visuals.title: Where CKD does its damage
visuals.text: Failing kidneys hit blood (anaemia), bone (fractures), heart and vessels (CVD, calcification) and parathyroids.

facts.label: Urine ACR is the first-line test
Bilateral shrinkage on ultrasound = CKD not AKI

visual.label: eGFR 38 = Stage 3b
visual.caption: Stages 1 and 2 only count as CKD with evidence of kidney damage.

Transfuse if Hb under 70 on RRT

glossary.Hyperkalaemia: A raised blood potassium level, which can cause dangerous heart rhythms.
glossary.Creatinine: A muscle waste product cleared by the kidneys; a rise means kidney function has fallen.
glossary.Urea: A nitrogen waste product of protein breakdown, cleared by the kidneys.
glossary.Oedema: Swelling caused by fluid collecting in the tissues.
glossary.Pallor: Unusual paleness of the skin, often from anaemia.
glossary.Polycystic kidney disease: An inherited disorder where many fluid-filled cysts grow in both kidneys and slowly destroy them.
glossary.Hypercalcaemia: A raised blood calcium level, causing constipation, abdominal pain and confusion.
glossary.Aortic flow murmur: A soft systolic murmur caused by fast blood flow through a normal aortic valve, as in anaemia.
glossary.Exertional dyspnoea: Breathlessness brought on by physical activity.
glossary.Tachycardia: A heart rate over 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Hb: Haemoglobin, the oxygen-carrying protein in red cells; a low level means anaemia.
glossary.Proximal myopathy: Weakness of the muscles nearest the trunk, such as hips and shoulders.
glossary.Waddling gait: A side-to-side walk caused by weak hip muscles.
glossary.Alendronic acid: A bisphosphonate drug that slows bone breakdown to protect against fractures.
glossary.Metformin: A first-line oral diabetes drug, avoided in significant CKD because of lactic acidosis risk.
glossary.Renal haematuria: Blood in the urine coming from the kidney itself rather than the lower urinary tract.
glossary.Histological: Relating to the microscopic structure of tissue, as seen on biopsy.
glossary.Creatinine clearance: The volume of blood cleared of creatinine per minute, used as an estimate of kidney filtration.
glossary.AKI: Acute kidney injury: a sudden fall in kidney function over hours to days, often reversible.
glossary.Renal ultrasound: A scan of the kidneys showing their size, shape and any blockage.
glossary.Mycobacterium tuberculosis: The bacterium that causes TB, screened for before transplant because immunosuppression can reactivate it.
glossary.Ramipril: An ACE inhibitor used to lower blood pressure and reduce proteinuria.
glossary.Lisinopril: An ACE inhibitor used to lower blood pressure and protect the kidneys.
glossary.ARB: Angiotensin receptor blocker, such as losartan; used instead of an ACE inhibitor if it is not tolerated.
glossary.Statin: A cholesterol-lowering drug such as atorvastatin, used to reduce cardiovascular risk.
glossary.Atorvastatin: A statin given to all CKD patients to lower cardiovascular risk.
glossary.NSAIDs: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs such as naproxen and ibuprofen; they can damage the kidneys.
glossary.Naproxen: An NSAID painkiller that can worsen kidney function.
glossary.Kidney transplant: Surgery placing a donor kidney into a patient with end-stage kidney failure; the definitive treatment.
glossary.Acute graft rejection: The immune system attacking a transplanted organ, usually within the first few months.
glossary.Ischaemic heart disease: Heart disease from narrowed coronary arteries; the commonest cause of death on haemodialysis.
glossary.Ferrous sulphate: An oral iron tablet used to treat iron deficiency.
glossary.IV iron: Iron given into a vein when oral iron is not enough or not absorbed.
glossary.SC: Subcutaneous: injected just under the skin.
glossary.Renal replacement therapy: Dialysis or transplant, used when the kidneys can no longer keep the patient alive.
glossary.RRT: Renal replacement therapy: dialysis or transplant.
glossary.Ergocalciferol: Vitamin D2, used to correct vitamin D deficiency.
glossary.Cholecalciferol: Vitamin D3, used to correct vitamin D deficiency.
glossary.Diuretics: Drugs that make the kidneys pass more salt and water, used for fluid overload.
glossary.Fluid overload: Too much fluid in the body, causing oedema and breathlessness.
glossary.Nephrons: The tiny filtering units of the kidney, about a million in each.
glossary.Erythropoiesis: The making of red blood cells in the bone marrow.
glossary.Peritubular fibroblasts: Cells around the kidney tubules that make erythropoietin.
glossary.Intraglomerular pressure: The pressure inside the glomerulus that drives filtration; too high damages it.
glossary.Hyperfiltration: Abnormally high filtration by remaining nephrons, which damages them over time.
glossary.Renoprotection: Protecting the kidneys from further damage.
glossary.Glycaemic control: How well blood glucose is kept in the target range.
